title: Private lifecycle safeguard and staged migration harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) need predictable, safe upgrades across a wide variety of topology and stateful deployments. Existing one-off scripts and ad-hoc flows lead to variable downtime, failed schema changes, and unclear rollback points. We need a principled upgrade harness that orchestrates staged rollouts, performs preflight checks, runs transactional migrations where possible, and provides a deterministic rollback path.
proposal: Build a 'Lifecycle Safeguard' subsystem that consists of three components: (1) Upgrade Controller (statemachine) that coordinates upgrade cohorts and rollout gates; (2) Migration Runner (idempotent, transactional step executor) that executes schema/data transformations with checkpoints and dry-run capability; (3) Preflight & Telemetry Layer that runs compatibility probes, KV/FS checks, and publishes a signed 'upgrade-plan' artifact for audit and rollback.
design_notes: Upgrade flows are declarative: an Upgrade manifest describes target runtime version, LTS channel, cohorts, preflight probes, and migration steps.
Cohort-based strategy: assign hosts/nodes into cohorts (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated health gates and manual approval hooks.
All migrations must be idempotent and record a checkpoint after each step; support dry-run mode against a replicated snapshot for schema-heavy steps.
Introduce a lightweight 'agent' on Private nodes that performs handshake with controller, streams logs, and can rollback locally on command.
Plan artifacts must be content-addressed and stored in customer-controlled storage (S3/GCS/NFS) to satisfy air-gapped requirements.
Provide a simulation harness that can run a full upgrade plan in a sandbox to detect drift and incompatible compound changes.

Telemetry: expose per-step latency, error rate, preflight probe results, and a migration digest to the Console (for Dedicated/Hosted customers this is aggregated; for Private we ship telemetry optionally with opt-in).
acceptance_criteria: Operators can create an Upgrade manifest and start a staged rollout against a VPC customer cluster
Controller enforces cohort gates and stops rollout on failing health checks
Migration Runner supports dry-run mode and records checkpoints for each step
Rollback can be executed (automated or manual) to the previous stable runtime and schema state within defined RPO
Upgrade plan artifact is stored and signed; an auditor can verify plan and results
End-to-end test (integration) that performs a canary upgrade on a 3-node cluster with synthetic traffic and validates no data loss
tasks: [Spike] Define Upgrade manifest schema and CRD (or declarative YAML) - 2d
Implement Upgrade Controller state machine and cohort scheduler - 8d
Build Migration Runner with idempotency and checkpoint semantics - 8d
Agent: lightweight orchestrator for on-prem nodes with streaming logs - 5d
Preflight probes: KV/FS checks, config compatibility, binary/LD_LIBRARY checks - 3d
Simulation harness: sandbox runner for dry-run upgrades - 6d
Console integration: surface plan status, step logs, and rollback actions - 4d
Security review and packaging for air-gapped installs - 2d
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running migrations cause service disruption. Mitigation: support online schema changes when possible, split migrations into small, reversible steps, allow traffic fencing and read-only windows.

Risk: Idempotency bugs cause double-applied migrations. Mitigation: require migration authorship guidelines, include checksum/digest verification, and introduce a dry-run stage against a point-in-time snapshot.
Risk: Agent-controller network partition. Mitigation: design agent for eventual reconciliation, local rollback commands, and a quarantine mode preventing partial upgrades.
Risk: Customer-specific state drift. Mitigation: include a preflight 'state fingerprint' and refuse to proceed if drift exceeds threshold; provide an investigative dry-run report.
